verdictProvider: No subagent judged anything in this round; the tester's own session ran every check, so no provider or model needs naming.

implementerProof.how: Recorded the server's real frame order and drove the reopen, offline, second close and typing cases in that order with my own throwaway Playwright spec, against the head web app and the 52159aaf web app; re-drove the unloadable close and rebuild that 312a14eb refactored.

proof.criterion: Review round 6: in the server's real frame order a read-only load stores and holds nothing, so a reopen, an offline spell and a second close show no false unsent-edit notice
proof.surface: Dispatch's Playwright harness (chromium and iphone) against the head's Go server, with a throwaway spec that records server frames and never reorders them (deleted after)
proof.command: Probe 0 recorded frames on a first connection and on a reconnect. Probe 2: agent spec with headings, closed; open; reopen; wait for the closed banner to go; cut, so the reconnect is writable; count rows; hold and cut (offline); read the status; close again; release; read the status and rows. bunx playwright test zz-tester-probe.e2e.ts --project chromium --project iphone --repeat-each 2 --workers 1 (DISPATCH_E2E_REUSE_SERVERS=1)
proof.observed: Frame order on both: Sync.Step1 > Sync.Step2 > Awareness > Auth > Sync.Step2. Probe 2, head, 4 of 4: 0 rows after the writable reconnect; offline status 'Connecting to the document…' with no edit named; after the second close the status is 'connected', with no notice and 0 rows.
proof.negativeControl: The 52159aaf web app (its connection.ts and pending-sync.ts) failed probe 2 2 of 2: 1 row stored after the reopen's reconnect, and the offline status read 'Connecting to the document… · 1 edit saved in this browser, not sent yet.' with nothing typed.

proof.criterion: A closed document stores nothing across reloads; typing after a reopen's reconnect survives a cut and a reload; another tab's row is restored
proof.command: Probe 1: a closed document opened, reconnected and reloaded twice, with the status and the row count after each. Probe 3: reopen, writable reconnect, hold and cut, type, reload, release. Probe 4: another tab's unsent row restored through a reopen's reconnect.
proof.observed: Head, 4 of 4 each. Probe 1: no notice and 0 rows every time. Probe 3: the status said 'saved in this browser, not sent yet' after the reload; the text reached the server; the rows cleared; no rebuild notice. Probe 4: the row reached the server with no rebuild notice.
proof.negativeControl: Probes 1, 3 and 4 also pass on 52159aaf, so the round's narrowing kept them working. Probe 2 is the case it changes, and it fails there.

proof.criterion: Server side after 312a14eb's refactor: a close beside an unloadable document succeeds, a rebuild shows the withdrawn block resolved, and a reopen opens it; closes withdraw every open ask; races stay consistent
proof.surface: dispatch:local at the head with the branch's CLI and the daemon's SetStatus
proof.command: TT-4: notes.md with an indexed block, its doc_updates corrupted in SQL, restart, daemonclose, rebuild as alice, reopen; seed.ts TT 3 with closes by alice, the agent CLI and SetStatus, then a reopen; race.ts resolve 8, double 5, unsettled 5, flip 5
proof.observed: Close 200; ask withdrawn; the log reads 'leave the ask blocks of a document whose history cannot load as they are'. Rebuild 200, block state="resolved"; after the reopen, state="open". The three closes give open_asks 0, the approval draft, and every open ask withdrawn naming its closer, with answered and retracted asks unchanged; the reopen restored 5 asks. Races: 0 problems.
proof.negativeControl: Round 5's control for the rebuild (the round-4 server 337c577d) left the block open; round 6's control for the closes (main 1357b95c) left open_asks 5.

correction: Round 7's gap probe let the authentication answer through ahead of the sync frames. The server sends Sync.Step1, Sync.Step2 and Awareness before Auth, so that probe tested an order the server never produces. Round 8's probes keep the server's own order.
